  June 12, 2026
Date: _________________
   CITY OF AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION

MEETING DATE:  June 17, 2026  AGENDA ITEM:
  2
PREPARED BY:  Kaden Likins, Contract Planner  APP TYPE(S): TRL

SUBJECT:  A Continued Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and
  Coastal Development Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or
  rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration at
  310 Catalina Avenue (PC#2915)

SUMMARY: A Continued Public Hearing considering a Transient Rental License and Coastal
Development Permit to allow renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than
thirty (30) consecutive days duration in the Multiple Residential – High Density (HD) zone at
310 Catalina Avenue. The Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 - Existing
Facilities). The proposed project is not located within the appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find this project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 under Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, because it
  has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 26-12 approving a Transient Rental License and Coastal
  Development Permit pursuant to PC#2915 (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a
authorize the Planning Commission to review and take action on applications for a Transient
Rental License and Coastal Development Permit.

BACKGROUND:

Application Information:

  Owner/Applicant  Jeff Souza
  Location  310 Catalina Avenue
  APN  7480-035-003
  General Plan  High Density Residential
  Land Use Designation
  Zoning Classification  Multiple Residential – High Density (HD)
  File Date  10/03/2025
   PC#2915 – 310 Catalina Avenue
  Page 2

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel addressed 310 Catalina Avenue. The
parcel is situated south of Beacon Street and north of Tremont Street, between Descanso
Avenue and Catalina Avenue. The lot is relatively flat, with a gentle slope from west to east.

The project site is currently developed with a 1,928 square foot two-story duplex residence, with
308 Catalina Avenue located on the second floor, and 310 Catalina Avenue located on the first
floor. There are separate lockable exterior entrances to each unit. The first floor, 310 Catalina
Avenue, consists of two bedrooms, a kitchen, one bathroom, a laundry room, a living room and
a dining room. 310 Catalina Avenue totals approximately 936 square feet and has two exterior
entrances from the front of the property, one which enters into the dining room and the other
entering into the living room. There is also an exterior entrance on the eastern side of the building
into the laundry room. The second floor, 308 Catalina Avenue, is accessible from an exterior
staircase at the front of the property which leads to an entrance porch. The property contains
additional rear yard area, which consists of an impervious patio with a seating area and outdoor
barbeque. In addition, there is a detached garage that is used for storage. The rear yard area
as well as detached garage will not be accessible to transient guests. Originally constructed in
1931, the residence has had minor subsequent improvements.

Both units have been part-time owner occupied as a vacation home in which family members
would use both units to visit the island. 308 Catalina Avenue will continue to be used as an
   PC#2915 – 310 Catalina Avenue
  Page 3

owner-occupied vacation home, while 310 Catalina Avenue is proposed to be rented on a
transient basis.

All abutting properties are in the HD zone and represent a mix of one- and two-story residential
buildings. A vicinity map, including adjacent property types and existing short-term rental status,
is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

There are no entitlements previously granted for the project site.

The site has three different City permits for home improvement:

  •  Permit #137 – Reconstruct exterior front stair way (September, 2018)
  •  Permit #19096 – Combination permit for sewer lateral (September, 2018)
  •  Permit #20034 – Plumbing permit to replace sewer lateral (November, 2025)

All permit work has been completed, and there are no other active building permits or
applications for the subject property.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicant, Jeff Souza, proposes to short-term rent the unit on
the first floor as a single unit, addressed 310 Catalina Avenue. 310 Catalina Avenue consists of
two bedrooms, a kitchen, one bathroom, a laundry room, a living room and a dining room. The
unit totals approximately 936 square feet and has two exterior entrances from the front of the
property, one which enters into the dining room and the other entering into the living room. There
is also an exterior entrance on the eastern side of the building into the laundry room. The second-
floor unit, 308 Catalina Avenue, is proposed to continue to be used as an owner-occupied
vacation home. The exterior rear yard area as well as the detached garage structure will not be
available to transient rental guests. The maximum occupancy of the unit will be six (6) individuals
based on the bedroom count and license limitations set forth in AMC Section 3-1.317.g. The
applicant does not propose an Autoette to be available to transient renters, and per condition
number 5, properties in the Flats are not permitted to have Autoette transportation available to
transient renters.

The proposed rental floor plan is included in Attachment 3 of this report.

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS: Staff has not identified any issue items for the proposed project.
It is in the opinion of Staff that existing regulations and standard conditions adequately address
potential nuisance concerns related to transient rental, and no additional conditions are required
to meet the findings required to grant the TRL for the property.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Pursuant AMC Section 3-1.310 and 9-8.103.d, recommended findings for approval of a
Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit are provided in draft Resolution No.
26-12 (Attachment 1).

Annual Growth Policy
   PC#2915 – 310 Catalina Avenue
  Page 4

The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2026 Annual Growth Policy.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing,
licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project
involves permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion
of the residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set for in
Avalon Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses.
As such, the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the
surrounding area.

Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the
exemptions as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2
and the Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for
the project. The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical
concern, does not result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the
environment due to unusual circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state
scenic highway, is not a hazardous waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: On May 8, 2026, the City sent a Public
Hearing Notice to owners/tenants within a 300-foot radius of the project site. The Hearing Notice
was published in Catalina Islander on May 8, 2026. The notice was posted at the project site
and in two additional locations on the same date. At the May 20th, 2026, regulation meeting,
the Planning Commission moved to continue the public hearing to the June 17th, 2026, regular
meeting due to the Commission not having a sufficient quorum present.

ATTACHMENTS:

  1. Draft Resolution No. PC 26-12
  2. Vicinity Map
  3. Floor Plan
   PC#2915 - ATTACHMENT 1

DRAFT RESOLUTION NO. PC 26-12
   RESOLUTION NO. PC 26-12

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  AVALON APPROVING A TRANSIENT RENTAL LICENSE AND
  COASTAL DEVELOPMENT PERMIT FOR ONE UNIT ADDRESSED 310
  CATALINA AVENUE AT THE EXISTING MULTI-FAMILY
  RESIDENTIAL DUPLEX LOCATED AT 310 CATALINA AVENUE (PC
  #2915)

  WHEREAS, Jeff Souza (“Applicant”) filed an application (“Application”) for a Transient
Rental License and Coastal Development Permit (PC#2915) to allow renting or leasing of a room
or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days duration (“Project”) for one unit of
the residential duplex property, addressed 310 Catalina Avenue, APN 7480-035-003 (“Site”); and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has authority per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC)
Sections 3-1.309 and 9-8.103.a to review and take action on the subject applications for a Transient
Rental License and a Coastal Development Permit; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is categorized High Density Residential by the General Plan Land
Use Element and is located within the designated area of the Multiple Family, High Density (HD)
zoning district as defined by AMC Section 9-5.406; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is located within the Coastal Zone and is within the planning
boundaries of the Avalon Local Coastal Program; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted one duly advertised public hearing on
June 17, 2026, at which time interested persons had an opportunity to testify either in support of
or opposition to granting a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit upon
property described in attached Exhibit “A”; and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites for the approval of the Transient Rental License
and Coastal Development Permit have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Planning Commission of the City of
Avalon does hereby approve a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit to allow
renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days
duration for the duplex unit addressed 310 Catalina Avenue, based on the following findings:

SECTION 1 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it
has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.
The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing,
or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project involves

  1
 permitting short-term rental use for an existing residential unit, involving no expansion of the
residential use on the project site, in compliance with all operational regulations set forth in Avalon
Municipal Code Chapter 3-1, Business Licensing, Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses. As such,
the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact on the surrounding area.
Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the exemptions
as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2 and the
Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for the project.
The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical concern, does not
result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual
circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state scenic highway, is not a hazardous
waste site, and is not identified as a historical resource.

SECTION 2 – FINDINGS
Transient Rental License
The proposed project may be granted a Transient Rental License for short-term rental per AMC
Chapter 3-1 (Business Licensing) Article 3 (Transient Rental Licenses). AMC Section 3-1.310 sets
forth the required findings for approval of a Transient Rental License as follows:
  a) The Planning Commission may, with such conditions as are deemed necessary, approve a
  Transient Rental License which will not jeopardize, adversely affect, endanger or
  otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general welfare, or be
  materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the vicinity of such use.
  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals, as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317, have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No additional special
  conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the transient rental license
  operational regulations.
  b) In making such determination, the Planning Commission shall find that the proposed
  transient rental use is in general accord with the following principles and standards:
  1)  The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings and structures
  shall be considered and no proposed transient rental use shall be permitted where
  such use will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses,
  buildings and structures;
  The subject property is an existing two-story duplex residence located within a
  predominantly residential area. No modifications to the property are proposed that
  would alter the ability of the building to function as a residence in the future. The
  property was inspected by the Planning and Building Department prior to the public
  hearing, and no health and safety issues were identified by the inspector that would
  prevent the residence from being used as a transient rental. Standard conditions of
  approval ensure that the operation of the transient rental will remain orderly and
  not have an adverse effect on surrounding residential properties.

  2
 2)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be adequate in size and shape to
  accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities, landscaping,
  outdoor entertaining areas and other development features prescribed in this
  chapter or as required as a condition in order to integrate said use and not be
  detrimental with the uses in the neighborhood;
  The project site is currently developed as a two-story multi-family duplex
  residence. The first floor, located at 310 Catalina Avenue, consists of two
  bedrooms, a kitchen, one bathroom, a laundry room, a living room and a dining
  room. 310 Catalina Avenue totals approximately 936 square feet and has multiple
  exterior entrances, two from the front of the property, one which enters into the
  dining room and the other entering into the living room. There is also an exterior
  entrance on the eastern side of the building into the laundry room. The second floor,
  located at 308 Catalina Avenue, is accessible from an exterior staircase at the front
  of the property which leads to an entrance porch. There is also an exterior staircase
  on the eastern side of the building which provides access to the second-floor unit,
  308 Catalina Avenue, into the laundry room.
  Transient renters would have access to the first-floor unit, addressed 310
  Catalina Avenue. There is also a rear yard patio and detached garage, in which
  transient renters will not have access to the rear yard patio or detached garage.
  Both units have been used as part-time owner-occupied vacation home in which
  family members would use both units to visit the island. The applicant does not
  plan to provide an Autoette for use by transient guests.
3)  The site for a proposed transient rental use shall be served by highways and streets
  adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity of
  traffic such use would generate.
  The project site is located towards the middle of Catalina Avenue between Beacon
  Street and Tremont Street. Eucalyptus Avenue is to the north and Descanso Avenue
  is to the south. This is a heavily traveled area by both vehicles and pedestrians.
  Tremont Street located to the west, is identified as Major Circulation Facility in the
  General Plan Circulation Element. It is anticipated that existing sidewalks and
  roadways, combined with the fact a vehicle will not be provided to transient guests,
  will ensure that traffic associated with operation of the business will not interfere
  with circulation along Catalina Avenue or Tremont Street.
4)  That the transient rental use must be ancillary to the residential use of residential
  unit, and would not create a commercial use in a residential zone. Whether a use
  is for a commercial use may be determined by the number of transient rental
  licenses previously granted to the applicant, the applicant's reason for the license
  and the nature of the requested license and any other factors presented in the
  application or at the hearing.
  The applicant currently does not operate any other transient rentals within the city.
  According to the owners, both units have been used as part-time owner-occupied
  vacation home in which family members would use both units to visit the island.

  3
   308 Catalina Avenue will continue to be used as an owner-occupied vacation home,
  while 310 Catalina Avenue is proposed to be rented on a transient basis.
  No modifications are proposed to the residence that would intensify the use of the
  property or alter the ability of the residence to function as a duplex residence in the
  future.
c) Conditions imposed by the Planning Commission for a Transient Rental License may
  involve any pertinent factors affecting the establishment, operation and maintenance of the
  requested transient rental use, including, but not limited to:
  1) Special yards, open spaces and buffer areas;
  2) Fences and walls;
  3) Parking facilities, including vehicular ingress and egress and the surfacing of parking
  area and driveways to specified standards;
  4) Street and highway dedications and improvements including sidewalks, curbs and
  gutters;
  5) Water supply and fire protection;
  6) Landscaping and maintenance of grounds;
  7) Regulation of nuisance factors such as noise, vibrations, smoke, dust, dirt, odors, gases,
  noxious matter, heat, glare, electromagnetic disturbances and radiation;
  8) Regulation of operating hours for activities affecting normal neighborhood schedules
  and functions;
  9) Regulation of signs, including outdoor advertising; and
  10) Such other conditions as will make possible the development of the proposed transient
  rental use in an orderly and efficient manner and in general accord with all elements
  of the General Plan and the intent and purpose of this chapter.
  Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals, as set forth in AMC Section 3-
  1.317, have been incorporated into the approval of the project. No security plan is
  required for renting one of the two units of the multi-family duplex residence, as all
  areas not accessible to transient renters will contain separate lockable entrances. No
  additional special conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the
  transient rental license operational regulations.
d) The Planning Commission shall deny the requested Transient Rental License where:
  1) The findings indicate, and the Commission determines, that the applicant has failed to
  show that the requested transient rental use will not jeopardize, adversely affect.
  endanger or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use, and reasonable restrictions or conditions to license the
  establishment of the proposed use will not prevent detriment or menace as indicated.
  Pursuant to AMC Section 3-1.310.a-c, the required findings have been made to
  determine that the proposed transient rental will not jeopardize, adversely affect,
  endanger, or otherwise constitute a menace to the public health, safety, or general
  welfare or be materially detrimental to the property of other persons located in the
  vicinity of such use. Standard conditions of approval for all transient rentals, as set

  4
   forth in AMC Section 3-1.317, have been incorporated into the approval of the project.
  No additional special conditions are required in order to ensure compliance with the
  transient rental license operational regulations.
  2) The applicant fails to attend the hearing of the Planning Commission in person or
  virtually, unless a valid excuse is provided.
  The applicant confirmed with Staff their intent to be in attendance at the public hearing
  prior to the publication of the meeting agenda.
  3) The applicant has previously had a Transient Rental License revoked for failure to
  maintain such license in good standing or for violation of the Municipal Code or any
  condition of the permit or had a conditional use permit revoked for violation of any
  requirement of this Municipal Code or violation of any condition of approval of the
  permit.
  The applicant has not had a business license, conditional use permit, or transient rental
  license for transient occupancy in the past, nor has any such license revoked for
  violations of the Municipal Code.
  4) The applicant previously operated a transient rental without a Transient Rental
  License. In deciding whether to deny the Transient Rental License on this basis, the
  Planning Commission may determine, in its reasonable discretion, whether substantial
  evidence supports that the applicant was not acting in bad faith when engaging in an
  illegal transient rental operation based upon: (1) the length of time that the operator
  failed to obtain a valid transient rental, (2) the length of time between when the
  operator was notified of the illegal operation and the time when the operator applied
  for a license, (3) whether the operator immediately discontinued illegal transient rental
  operation upon notice, (4) whether only one transient rental unit was operated, and (5)
  whether the operator was a sophisticated party, meaning the operator or its affiliates
  have engaged in transient rental operation previously. The applicant has the burden of
  presenting evidence that prior illegal transient rental operation was not conducted
  deliberately or in bad faith.
  The applicant has not previously operated a transient rental without a license within the
  City.
  5) The property proposed for transient rental use is out of compliance with any
  requirement of this Municipal Code at the time the Planning Commission hears the
  application.
  The project site is not subject to any active code enforcement cases and is otherwise in
  good standing with licensing and permitting requirements with the City of Avalon.
e) In addition to the foregoing, the Planning Commission shall consider the following in
  connection with an application for a Transient Rental License:
  1) Year-Round Rental Status. In the absence of adequate mitigating measures proposed
  by the applicant, the application should be denied where the subject property is or has
  been rented for periods of more than 30 consecutive days to the same occupant at any
  time during the two years preceding the application.

  5
   Staff has found no evidence that the subject property has been rented for 30 or more
  consecutive days or more to the same occupant in the last two years. According to the
  owners, the property has been used as a part-time owner occupied vacation home in
  which family members would use both units to visit the island. 308 Catalina Avenue
  will continue to be used as an owner-occupied vacation home, while 310 Catalina
  Avenue is proposed to be rented on a transient basis.
2) Neighborhood Impacts. The Planning Commission shall consider the objections of the
  owners and occupants of neighboring properties in determining whether the proposed
  transient rental use is consistent with the surrounding properties and the extent to
  which such impacts may be mitigated by the imposition of the standard conditions listed
  below or by the imposition of additional conditions. The Planning Commission may
  consider objections previously made in connection with applications for transient
  rental use at other properties located within the same general area as the subject
  application; however, the Planning Commission should consider the time between the
  prior application and the subject application, the geographical proximity of the subject
  application to the prior application, any differing circumstances, and additional
  mitigating measures proposed by the applicant, and changes in the general area, in
  determining the weight to be given such prior objections.
  No objection letters were received by the Planning and Building Department prior to
  the publication of the meeting agenda.
3) Condominium Associations Having IO or More Units. In the case of an application
  concerning property located within a condominium or similar congregate housing
  project consisting of 10 or more units, the applicant shall be required to provide written
  approval from the governing body of the subject association consenting to the
  allowance of the transient rental use at the condominium or congregated housing
  project.
  The project site is not located within a condominium or homeowners association.
4) The Planning Commission shall consider whether granting the Transient Rental
  License shall result in any year round residence located adjacent to the proposed
  transient rental having more than a majority of the adjacent residences permitted or
  licensed for transient rental use. "Adjacent" means having a common property line with
  the proposed transient rental unit except for the existence of a public street or alley.
  The total square footage of the dwelling unit and the site of each bedroom shall be
  considered for determining whether to grant the Transient Rental License.
  The vicinity map prepared for the project, included as Attachment 2 of the staff report,
  shows that granting of the transient rental license will not result in year round
  residences located adjacent to the proposed transient rental having more than a majority
  of the adjacent residences permitted or licensed for transient rental use.
  310 Catalina Avenue is currently located next to a licensed transient rental property on
  the western side. There are no licensed properties adjacent to the rear consist along
  Descanso Avenue. Adjacent to the western side is 312 Catalina Avenue which is a
  licensed transient rental property. Adjacent to the eastern side is 306 Catalina Avenue,

  6
   which is not a licensed transient rental property, which will not be surrounded by
  majority of lots with transient rental licenses. Across the public right of way to the
  north are multiple non-licensed transient rental properties, 305, 307, 309, 311 and 313
  Catalina Avenue, which will not have majority of adjacent properties as licensed
  transient rental properties, as properties to the rear along Eucalyptus Avenue are not
  licensed transient rental properties. Additional applicable surrounding properties are
  not licensed to rent transiently.
  The subject property is approximately 2,299 square feet in size, constructed with an
  approximate 1,928 square foot multi-family deplex residence, which is within the
  average size range for a multi-family duplex residences within the Flats. The floor plan
  of the building is standard for a duplex residence, and the placement of the bedrooms
  does not provide cause for concern with granting the TRL.
  f) The Planning Commission shall impose as a condition all of the requirements and
  standards set forth in § 3-1.317, plus such additional conditions which the Planning
  Commission determines are appropriate to mitigate the impacts of such transient rental
  use.
  Required and recommended conditions of approval have been included as an attachment
  to this Resolution. No additional conditions are recommended by the Planning
  Commission.
Coastal Development Permit
The City of Avalon is located entirely within the Coastal Zone. The project is not located within
the 300-foot appealable boundary of the Coastal Zone and qualifies as an increase in the intensity
of use that requires issuance a Coastal Development Permit per AMC Section 9-8.102.b.2.v, on
the following findings:
  1. The use is in conformance with the certified Local Coastal Program. (AMC 9-
  8.103.d.1)
  Determination of conformance for projects within the City of Avalon includes analysis of
  whether the proposed project conforms with the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal
  Plan for Avalon, as well as the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances, as
  applicable.
  •  General Plan/Local Coastal Plan: The Multiple Family, High Density Residential (HD)
  zoning designation of the project site is consistent with the General Plan land use
  designation of High Density Residential.
  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Goals and Policies:
  Policies II-20 and II-21 of the Land Use Element:
  “Pursue new developments and businesses that add to the City’s economic base,
particularly those that general sales tax and transient occupancy tax.”
  “Expand lodging choices by attracting and retaining desirable and high-quality facilities
  to the community.”

  7
   The City recognizes that short-term rentals contribute significantly to economic
  development, allow visitors to experience the unique island community of Avalon, and
  assist in providing access to the coast. Permitting and regulation of short-term rentals
  through the Transient Rental License process allows the City to monitor rental activity to
  ensure their operation has minimal negative impact to surrounding properties and also
  provides a significant income from transient occupancy tax, which is paid monthly to the
  City.
  •  Avalon Local Coastal Program (LCP): The Avalon Local Coastal Program (LCP)
  emphasizes the fact that Avalon is a visitor-focused community, with multiple
  visitor-serving facilities and recreational opportunities. Availability of short-term
  rentals provides access to alternative forms of accommodation for visitors to the
  community within existing developed properties, supplementing the need for new
  visitor-serving development. Continued permitting and management of short-term
  rentals in the community is consistent with the intent of the LCP and implements
  Sections 30213 and 30222 of the California Coastal Act.
  •  HD Zone Development Standards: The proposed project does not involve any
  modifications or additions to an existing building that require analysis pursuant to
  the development standards for the HD zone. No adjustments or variances are
  required to permit the proposed project.
  •  Affordable Housing Ordinance: This ordinance is not applicable to the proposed
  project since the proposal does not include the development of five or more
  residential units.
  2. For all development seaward of the nearest public highway to the shoreline, the
  proposed development conforms to the public access and recreation policies of
  Chapter 3 of the Coastal Act. (AMC 9-8.103.d.2)
  The project site is not seaward of Crescent Avenue, which is the nearest public access to
  the shoreline. The proposed project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
  developed residential property in a residential area of the city, in compliance with
  development standards for the HD zone and Transient Rental License regulations.
  Therefore, the project does not involve a change in land use, density, or intensity that will
  result in increased demand for public access and recreation opportunities. Furthermore, the
  project does not include any building or site modification that could block or impede
  existing public access opportunities.
Annual Growth Policy
The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The project involves permitting short-term rental use of an existing
residential unit, with no modifications to the floor plan or bedroom count. Water demand for
residential buildings is calculated based on the number of bedrooms in the unit. Since the floor
plan of the unit is not impacted, the project is not subject to evaluation of an allocation for water
service. Therefore, Staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2026 Annual Growth Policy.

1. Registration, Inspection, and Licensing Requirements.

  a. Any managing agency, agent, owner or property manager who rents one or more
  transient rentals shall be required to obtain a City business license. Failure to obtain
  a business license or continuing to operate a transient rental after revocation of a
  business license constitutes a misdemeanor pursuant to § 1-2.01 of the Municipal
  Code, and may result in imposition of a fine upon conviction, among other
  penalties.

  b. All transient rentals shall be subject to collection of transient occupancy tax as
  required by the Municipal Code, and each managing agency, agent, owner, and
  property manager of a transient rental shall collect and make payment to the City
  of the transient occupancy tax for their transient rental.

2. Sign Requirements. Each transient rental unit shall have posted in a location that is clearly
  visible from the outside of the property one sign with the contents set forth below. The sign
  shall either be purchased at a reasonable cost through the City of Avalon Planning
  Department or consistent with a template provided by the City. The sign shall be made of
  material which affixes to a window, not to exceed two square feet in size, have lettering of
  sufficient size to be easily read from a place accessible to the public, and shall clearly
  contain the following information:

  a. Street address of the transient rental unit;
  b. Allowed maximum occupancy for the transient rental unit;
  c. Name of the managing agency, agent, property manager, or owner of the unit, and
  a local telephone number at which that property manager or his agent may be
  reached on a twenty-four-hour basis; and
  d. City of Avalon Business License Number

3. Advertising Requirements. Any sign or online posting advertising the available use of a
  transient rental unit must meet all of the advertising and sign requirements found in the
  Avalon Municipal Code, including identification of the property's City of Avalon Business
  License Number.

4. Notice and Rental Agreement Requirements.

  a. Upon check-in, the managing agency, agent, property manager, owner of the unit,
  or other designee must meet all transient rental guests in person prior to providing
  access to the property to review rental regulations and verify the number of guests
  arriving are in compliance with the unit's occupancy limits.

  12
   i. The managing agency, agent, property manager, owner of the unit, or other
  designee must maintain a valid City of Avalon Business License.

  b. Each transient rental unit shall have a clearly visible and legible notice posted
  within the unit on or adjacent to the front door, containing the following
  information:

  i. The name of the managing agency, agent, property manager, or owner of
  the unit, and a local telephone number at which that party or his/her agent
  may be reached on a twenty-four-hour basis;
  ii. The maximum number of occupants permitted to stay in the unit;
  iii. Notification that trash and refuse shall not be left or stored on the property,
  the scheduled dates and times for pick-up at the location, and an explanation
  of the City's recycling program;
  iv. Notification that failure to conform to the parking and occupancy
  requirements of the structure is a violation of this section;
  v. When the City has enacted water conservancy measures by ordinance,
  notice of the requirements of such ordinance and a request that occupants
  conserve water as much as possible in the use of showers, baths, faucets,
  and laundry;
  vi. Notification that use of unenclosed decks and patios between 8:00 p.m. and
  8:00 a.m. is prohibited where such use generates noise which would disturb
  or annoy a reasonable person occupying the adjacent properties; and
  vii. A statement that Avalon has a "zero tolerance" policy towards nuisances,
  rowdy and disruptive behavior, and advising that the occupancy will be
  immediately terminated for violations of this policy.

  c. The foregoing information shall be stated in the rental information and agreement
  provided to prospective renters prior to their occupancy of the unit.

5. Vehicles. Off-street parking shall be provided on or off site such that all vehicles bearing
  permits issued for the unit can be parked off street, except when used pursuant to a
  temporary permit issued to the owner as provided in Title 4. The owner, agent, and
  managing agency shall comply with the Avalon vehicle ordinance which (1) permits
  transient renters to only use the vehicle which is permitted for the location; and (2) prohibits
  the owner, agent or managing agency from charging for the use of the vehicle, except:

  a. Properties located in the "flats" (as defined in§ 9-5.406) and properties located in
  the condominium known as "Bahia Vista," "Canyon Terrace," and "Sol Vista" shall
  not include a vehicle to be used by transient guests.

6. Trash. The owner or managing agent shall provide written information to each transient
  occupant setting out the schedule for trash pick-up at the location and an explanation of the
  City's recycling program and ensure that there are adequate materials for disposing of trash

  13
   in accordance with the City's program. All trash containers shall be secured against animal
  incursion.

7. Maximum Occupancy. The maximum occupancy for transient rentals shall be two persons
  (including children and infants) per bedroom, plus two; provided the Planning Commission
  in its discretion may establish a different maximum number where appropriate and
  reasonable to permit fewer persons that the foregoing formula might otherwise allow and
  may also increase the number that would otherwise be allowed under the foregoing formula
  where facts are presented demonstrating that the configuration of the property warrants it.
  Reasons for establishing a different maximum occupancy number include, but are not
  limited to:

  a. Size and location of the property;
  b. Distinction between single- and multi-unit properties; and
  c. Number and size of each sleeping room in the transient rental unit.

8. Unenclosed Areas. The use of unenclosed areas, such as decks and balconies, attached to
  each transient rental unit shall be prohibited between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.
  Monday through Sunday.

9. Noise. The occupants of the transient rental shall at all times remain in compliance with
  the Noise Ordinance as outlined in Chapter 5-13 of this Municipal Code.

10. Code Compliance, Fire Safety, and Inspection. Each dwelling unit used for transient rental
  within the City is subject to all of the following inspection requirements:

  a. The owner shall be responsible for compliance with all codes regarding Fire,
  Building and Safety, Health and Safety, and other relevant laws and the
  requirements of these Conditions of Approval.

  b. The transient rental unit shall be inspected prior to commencement of the use,
  which inspection shall be scheduled and conducted within 30 days of approval. In
  addition to the registration for each unit as required in subsection (a) of this section,
  an original, signed inspection report for each unit shall be submitted to the Director
  of Finance in order to obtain approval to use the unit as a transient rental.
  Inspections shall be conducted by a qualified inspector(s) authorized and approved
  by the City to conduct such inspections. Inspectors shall demonstrate appropriate
  qualifications to conduct the required inspections as determined by the Building
  Official or the Fire Department, as applicable. The cost of such inspections, plus
  any administrative charges, shall be paid by the owner pursuant to the City's
  adopted fee schedule. The City shall make every reasonable effort to ensure that
  inspections are completed in a timely manner. Within 15 days following inspection,
  the inspectors shall submit an original, signed inspection report to the Planning
  Department, or, where applicable, provide notice that the property owner has
  unreasonably prevented inspection. Failure to cooperate with the scheduling of

  14
   inspection shall subject the approval to use the unit as a transient rental to
  revocation.

c. After the initial inspection, each rental unit shall be reinspected no less than once
  every three years following the original inspection. Verification of inspection will
  be done at the time of business license renewal. Failure to submit inspection reports
  shall result in revocation of approval to use the unit for transient rentals.

d. Inspections shall verify compliance with all applicable provisions of this section.

e. If upon completing an inspection of a transient rental, the inspector(s) determines
  that the unit is not in conformance with this section, the inspector shall provide the
  managing agency, agent, owner, or property manager with a list of required
  corrections, set a reasonable time for correction and a date for reinspection. A copy
  of the foregoing shall also be given to the Planning Department. If the unit is
  registered with the City as a transient rental, approval by the City to use the unit for
  transient rental shall be suspended until correction and reinspection if determined
  by the inspector to present an immediate health and safety hazard, and submission
  of a new inspection report for the unit indicating compliance with this section. If
  the unit is not yet registered with or approved by the City, approval for its use as a
  transient rental shall be withheld until submission of a new inspection report for the
  unit indicating compliance with this section.

f. Noncompliance by an owner, managing agency, property manager or agent of the
  requirements for registration, inspection and operation of transient rentals may
  result in the revocation of the business license and Transient Rental License
  authorizing the use, and upon revocation, no new business license or Transient
  Rental License may be issued to the same transient rental licensee for a period of
  12 months following such revocation.

g. The following requirements for transient rentals will be evaluated upon inspection
  of each unit, and shall constitute minimum requirements. The unit must be brought
  into conformance with these requirements and any other applicable codes and
  ordinances in order for the use to be allowed.

  i. Required sign and notice must be posted, and address of unit must be legible
  from outside the property unless exempted.
  ii. Smoke detectors shall be installed within each sleeping room and at a point
  centrally located in the corridor or area giving access to each separate
  sleeping room. Battery-operated smoke detectors are acceptable, provided
  that they are maintained in good working order at all times, or except as
  required by other applicable codes. Where fire suppression systems have
  been installed, such systems shall also be subject to the inspection and
  testing requirements set forth in Title 4, Chapter 3.

  15
   iii. The transient rental shall be equipped with a minimum of one 2A: I 0B:C
  type extinguisher with 75 feet of travel distance to all portions of the
  structure; there shall be no less than one such extinguisher per floor. Fire
  extinguishers shall be mounted in visible locations with the tops of the
  extinguishers mounted between three feet and five feet above the floor and
  shall be accessible to occupants at all times. California State Fire Marshal
  annual certification tags must be provided and be current on all
  extinguishers.
  iv. Any locking mechanism on outside doors must be operable from inside the
  unit without the use of a key. If the dwelling unit is greater than 3,000 square
  feet in area, two exit doors shall be required, each of which shall conform
  to this requirement.
  v. Transient rentals shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition and
  free from hazards, which shall include meeting the following requirements:
  1. There shall be no exposed wiring, improper wiring materials, or
  overloaded electrical circuits;
  2. There shall be no permanent use of extension cords for appliances,
  heaters, lamps, or other fixtures;
  3. There shall be no leaking fixtures, clogged or leaking wastewater
  lines;
  4. Faucets and fixtures shall be maintained in working conditions;
  5. Showers, sinks, and bathing facilities shall be clean and properly
  maintained;
  6. There shall be no evidence of pest infestations;
  7. If directed by the Fire Department, bedroom windows shall be
  operable to allow for emergency egress;
  8. There shall be at least one window per bedroom, to allow for proper
  interior ventilation;
  9. There shall be no accumulation of trash and/or debris on the site or
  within the unit;
  10. All steps, stairways, decks, and railings shall be stable and
  structurally sound;
  11. All standard appliances, including but not limited to kitchen
  appliances, furnaces, and water heaters, shall be operational;
  12. Any hot tubs, pools, and spas shall be fenced or equipped with an
  approved cover with locking mechanisms as required by State law,
  and shall be maintained in a safe and sanitary condition;
  13. Any lofts or attic conversions shall be provided with acceptable
  exiting and head clearance; stairs or providing access to these areas
  shall be safe and structurally sound; and
  14. Exits shall remain clear of storage, debris, or impedance at all times.

h. The managing agency, agent, property manager, or owner of the unit whose name
  and local telephone number appears on the sign pursuant to subsection (b) of this
  section or pursuant to a conditional use permit and/or who is identified in the
  Transient Rental License must maintain a physical presence within the

  16
   geographical limits of the City of Avalon during the term of the transient rental unit
  lease in order to provide response to complaints within 30 minutes of notification.
  Failure to be available or failure to answer the telephone shall be deemed the same
  as failure to respond.

11. Annual Minimum Stay. Any managing agency, agent, owner, or property manager who
  rents one or more transient rentals shall be required to ensure a minimum stay of at least
  ten (10) nights in each transient rental per calendar year.
